label: multi-store refactor + voided-join lint + count-orders example

results.question: How many orders have been placed?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS total_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided';
results.answer: Your shop has received a total of 17,340 orders. This count includes all non-voided orders across your entire sales history. Please note that this total assumes all past records are fully up to date and correctly marked in the system.
results.assumptions: Counting all non-voided orders across the entire date range.

results.question: What is our total revenue?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided';
results.answer: Your total revenue for the period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, was $3,321,930.71 AUD. This figure includes all non-voided orders across the entire dataset.
results.assumptions: Calculated total revenue as the sum of 'total' for all non-voided orders across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: How many different products do we sell?
results.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT product_id) AS total_products FROM products WHERE status = 'active';
results.answer: You currently sell 42 different products in your active catalogue as of today, September 30, 2026. This count includes all items currently marked as active, though it may exclude discontinued or archived items.
results.assumptions: Counting all active products in the product catalogue as of today (2026-09-30).

results.question: How many physical store locations do we have?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS physical_store_count FROM locations WHERE type = 'pos'
results.answer: You have 2 physical store locations based on your point-of-sale data. This count only includes locations specifically marked with the "pos" store type.
results.assumptions: Counting locations where type is 'pos' (physical point-of-sale stores).

results.question: What is the average order value?
results.sql: SELECT round(avg(total), 2) AS average_order_value FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided';
results.answer: Your average order value is 191.58 AUD. This calculation covers all non-voided orders across the entire dataset period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Calculated the average order value across all non-voided orders for the entire dataset period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: How many orders were placed online versus in store?
results.sql: SELECT sales_channel, count(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY sales_channel ORDER BY sales_channel;
results.answer: Customers placed 10,667 orders online and 6,673 orders in-store across the available date range. These figures exclude any voided orders, assuming the provided dataset covers all valid transactions for both sales channels.
results.assumptions: Comparing online orders vs. in-store (POS) orders, excluding voided orders across the entire available date range.

results.question: Which product has the highest price?
results.sql: SELECT p.title, v.size, v.color, v.price FROM variants v JOIN products p USING (product_id) ORDER BY v.price DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: The product with the highest price is the Trench Coat (size XS in Cobalt) at $269.95 AUD. This is based on the current GST-inclusive price found in the provided catalogue data.
results.assumptions: Found the variant with the highest current GST-inclusive price in the catalogue.

results.question: How many refunds have been issued?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS total_refunds FROM refunds;
results.answer: You have issued a total of 988 refunds through the system. This count represents individual refund events recorded to date. Please note that this total assumes all recorded transactions in the system are accurate and up to date.
results.assumptions: Counting total individual refund events recorded in the system.

results.question: How many units have we sold in total?
results.sql: SELECT sum(l.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: You sold a total of 32,871 units across all non-voided orders. This count covers the entire available date range from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. Please note that this total assumes all recorded transactions in the system during this period are complete and accurate.
results.assumptions: Counting total units sold across all non-voided orders for the entire dataset range (Oct 1, 2025 to Sep 30, 2026).

results.question: List all the discount codes.
results.sql: SELECT code, title, kind, value, is_automatic, starts_on, ends_on FROM discounts ORDER BY code;
results.answer: You have 10 discount codes set up in your system, which include percentage-off deals like WELCOME10 (10%) and BLACKFRIDAY (25%), fixed-amount vouchers like EXPIRED5 ($5) and SAVE20 ($20), and a FREESHIP free shipping code. Please note that values are listed as percentages or fixed amounts in AUD depending on the discount type, and some codes like EXPIRED5 have already passed their end date.
results.assumptions: Retrieved all discount codes from the discounts table.

results.question: How many orders were placed on Saturdays?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS saturday_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND extract(isodow from (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) = 6
results.answer: There were 3,468 orders placed on Saturdays. This count includes only non-voided orders based on Australia/Sydney local time.
results.assumptions: Counting non-voided orders placed on Saturdays using Australia/Sydney local time.

results.question: How much revenue did we make in December 2025?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum(total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2025-12-01' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-01-01';
results.answer: Your total revenue for December 2025 was $350,341.05 AUD. This includes all non-voided orders placed during that month based on Australia/Sydney local time.
results.assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of orders.total for non-voided orders placed in December 2025, using Australia/Sydney local time.

results.question: How many orders were voided?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS voided_order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status = 'voided';
results.answer: You had a total of 143 voided orders across your available dataset. This count includes every order marked with a voided financial status. Please note that this total covers the entire history in the system without any date restrictions applied.
results.assumptions: Counting all orders where financial_status is 'voided' across the entire available dataset.

results.question: How many different colours do we stock?
results.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT color) AS total_colors FROM variants WHERE color IS NOT NULL;
results.answer: You currently stock 15 different colours. This total is based on counting the unique colour names recorded in your product variants table. This assumes all colour variations are correctly and uniquely spelled in your system.
results.assumptions: Counting unique colour values recorded in the variants table.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by units sold?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 5
results.answer: Your top-selling product by units is the One-Piece Swimsuit with 4,043 units sold, followed by the Straw Hat at 3,619, the Leather Belt at 2,667, the Linen Wrap Skirt at 1,804, and the Shirt Dress at 1,492. These figures cover all sales channels from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, with voided orders excluded.
results.assumptions: Top 5 products by total units sold across all channels, excluding voided orders over the entire available date range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What are our top 5 products by revenue?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, round(sum(l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5
results.answer: Your top 5 products by revenue are the One-Piece Swimsuit at $321,895.78 AUD, the Shirt Dress at $224,593.45 AUD, High-Rise Jeans at $184,912.94 AUD, the Wool Coat at $177,259.45 AUD, and the Straw Hat at $171,331.88 AUD. These figures represent total gross revenue across all sales channels, including GST and discounts, while excluding voided orders.
results.assumptions: Calculated total gross revenue (unit price * quantity minus line discounts, GST-inclusive) for each product across all channels, excluding voided orders.

results.question: What was our revenue in each month?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(total)::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;
results.answer: Your monthly revenue ranged from a low of $186,309.58 in February 2026 to a high of $367,315.71 in June 2026. Specifically, October 2025 was $207,445.04, November 2025 was $263,671.86, December 2025 was $350,341.05, January 2026 was $245,785.38, March 2026 was $240,875.20, April 2026 was $245,710.87, May 2026 was $312,026.08, July 2026 was $342,251.10, August 2026 was $282,129.97, and September 2026 was $278,068.87. These figures only include non-voided orders calculated in Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of orders.total for non-voided orders, grouped by calendar month in Australia/Sydney time.

results.question: Which month had the highest revenue, and how much was it?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Your highest revenue month was June 2026, bringing in $367,315.71 in gross sales. This total covers all non-voided orders from October 2025 through September 2026 based on Sydney local time.
results.assumptions: Interpreting revenue as gross revenue (orders.total) for non-voided orders, grouped by calendar month in Australia/Sydney time across the entire data range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: How much revenue came from each sales channel?
results.sql: SELECT sales_channel, round(sum(total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY sales_channel ORDER BY revenue DESC;
results.answer: Your online sales channel brought in $2,070,833.88 in revenue, while your in-store point of sale (pos) channel generated $1,251,096.83. These totals include all non-voided orders and are based on the total order amounts provided in the data.
results.assumptions: Revenue includes all non-voided orders grouped by sales channel (online vs. pos), using total order amount.

results.question: What is the revenue for each store location?
results.sql: SELECT l.name AS location_name, l.type AS location_type, ROUND(SUM(o.total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY l.location_id, l.name, l.type ORDER BY revenue DESC;
results.answer: Your total revenue by store location for the period from October 2025 through September 2026 is 2,070,833.88 AUD for the Online Store, 755,981.28 AUD for the Surry Hills Boutique, and 495,115.55 AUD for the Newtown Boutique. These figures include all non-voided orders across the entire available date range.
results.assumptions: Revenue is calculated as the sum of orders.total for non-voided orders, grouped by each store location across the entire available date range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: Compare the average order value for online and in-store orders.
results.sql: SELECT sales_channel, ROUND(AVG(total), 2) AS average_order_value, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY sales_channel ORDER BY sales_channel;
results.answer: Online orders had a slightly higher average order value of 194.13 AUD compared to in-store orders at 187.49 AUD. This comparison includes all non-voided orders across the entire dataset range from October 2025 through September 2026.
results.assumptions: Comparing average order value (AOV) across sales channels (online vs. pos/in-store) for all non-voided orders across the entire dataset range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: Which product type sells the most units?
results.sql: SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o USING (order_id) JOIN variants v USING (variant_id) JOIN products p USING (product_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Accessories sell the most units, with a total of 8,771 units sold. This result excludes voided orders, assuming all other recorded sales are final.
results.assumptions: Excluding voided orders. Grouping by product_type in lowercase as per schema guidelines.

results.question: Which day of the week do we get the most orders, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'Day') AS day_of_week, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1, EXTRACT(DOW FROM o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: You get the most orders on Saturdays, with a total of 3,468 orders. This is based on non-voided orders converted to Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Which day of the week do we get the most orders, and how many, based on non-voided orders converted to Australia/Sydney time.

results.question: At the peak hour of the day (Sydney time), how many online orders do we get in total?
results.sql: SELECT extract(hour from (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) as hour_of_day, count(o.order_id) as order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.sales_channel = 'online' AND o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Your peak hour for online orders is 8:00 PM Sydney time, with a total of 1,232 orders. This total covers all online orders from October 2025 through September 2026, and excludes any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Analyzed all online orders across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) converted to Australia/Sydney time, grouping by hour of the day and finding the peak hour by total order count. Voided orders are excluded.

results.question: How much have we given away in discounts in total?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(discount_total), 2) AS total_discounts_given FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: You have given away a total of $175,099.89 in discounts across all non-voided orders from the start of the data period through September 30, 2026. This total assumes all recorded discounts were successfully applied at checkout and excludes any voided transactions.
results.assumptions: Calculated total discounts given by summing discount_total across all non-voided orders from the start of the data period to today (2026-09-30).

results.question: How many orders used the most popular discount code?
results.sql: SELECT d.code, d.title, count(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM discounts d JOIN orders o ON d.discount_id = o.discount_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY d.code, d.title ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: The most popular discount code was BOXINGDAY (Boxing Day Sale 30% off), which was used in 1,081 orders. This count includes only non-voided orders across the full date range of the dataset.
results.assumptions: Counting non-voided orders associated with each discount code to find the most popular one, using the full date range of the dataset.

results.question: How many orders used the WELCOME10 code?
results.sql: SELECT count(o.order_id) AS welcome10_order_count FROM orders o JOIN discounts d ON o.discount_id = d.discount_id WHERE d.code = 'WELCOME10' AND o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: A total of 926 non-voided orders used the WELCOME10 code between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026. This count only includes completed transactions and excludes any orders that were subsequently voided.
results.assumptions: Counted all non-voided orders associated with the discount code WELCOME10 across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What is the total refunded amount for each refund reason?
results.sql: SELECT reason, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_refunded, COUNT(*) AS refund_count FROM refunds GROUP BY reason ORDER BY total_refunded DESC;
results.answer: The top refund reason is the wrong size at $48,751.06, followed by a change of mind at $32,511.66, faulty items at $15,383.14, items not as described at $14,787.06, and late arrivals at $5,199.00. These totals cover the entire available date range without any specific time filter applied.
results.assumptions: Grouped all refund records by their stated reason to calculate the total refunded amount and count for each over the entire available date range.

results.question: What is the most common reason for refunds, and how many refunds is that?
results.sql: SELECT reason, count(*) AS refund_count FROM refunds GROUP BY reason ORDER BY refund_count DESC LIMIT 1
results.answer: The most common reason for refunds is "Wrong size," with a total of 397 refund events. This count is based on the specific text entered in the reason field by customers.
results.assumptions: Counting the number of refund events grouped by the reason field.

results.question: Which state do most online orders ship to, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT shipping_state AS state, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE sales_channel = 'online' AND financial_status <> 'voided' AND shipping_state IS NOT NULL GROUP BY shipping_state ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Most of your online orders ship to New South Wales, with a total of 5,457 orders. This count excludes voided orders and those missing a shipping state.
results.assumptions: Excluding voided orders and orders with null shipping states. Counting non-voided online orders grouped by their shipping_state.

results.question: How many orders were placed during the Black Friday sale (27 Nov to 1 Dec 2025)?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2025-11-27 00:00:00' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') <= '2025-12-01 23:59:59'
results.answer: You received 468 orders during the Black Friday sale between 27 November and 1 December 2025. This total excludes any voided orders based on Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Date range 27 Nov to 1 Dec 2025 inclusive in Australia/Sydney time; excluded voided orders.

results.question: How much revenue did we make last month?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date >= '2026-08-01' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date <= '2026-08-31';
results.answer: You made a total gross revenue of $282,129.97 AUD last month (August 2026). This figure includes all non-voided orders processed during that period based on Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Treating today as 2026-09-30, 'last month' is August 2026 (2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31) in Australia/Sydney time. Revenue is gross revenue from non-voided orders.

results.question: How many customer accounts were created in 2026?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS customer_accounts_created FROM customers WHERE created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-01-01' AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2027-01-01';
results.answer: You had 1,109 new customer accounts created in 2026. This total is based on sign-ups recorded in Australian Eastern time during the 2026 calendar year.
results.assumptions: Counting customer sign-ups (customers.created_at) during the calendar year 2026 in Australia/Sydney time.

results.question: How many units did we sell in each size?
results.sql: SELECT v.size, sum(l.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.size IS NOT NULL GROUP BY v.size ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC;
results.answer: You sold a total of 32,871 units across all sizes between October 2025 and September 2026. The most popular size was "One Size" with 8,771 units, followed closely by Medium at 7,255 and Small at 6,745. The larger and smaller ends of the range were less common, with Large at 5,327, Extra Large at 2,412, and Extra Small at 2,361 units sold. These totals include all non-voided orders across the entire available date range.
results.assumptions: Calculated total units sold by variant size across all non-voided orders for the entire available data range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: How much revenue did our dresses bring in?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum(ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount), 2) AS dress_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND lower(p.product_type) = 'dress'
results.answer: Your dresses brought in a total of $542,989.65 in gross revenue. This figure covers all non-sold-out, non-voided dress orders from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026, including GST and applied discounts.
results.assumptions: Revenue includes all non-voided orders for products of type 'dress' across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Revenue is gross, GST-inclusive, and accounts for line discounts.

results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum(((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * l.quantity))::numeric, 2) AS gross_profit, round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue_ex_gst, round((sum(((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * l.quantity)) / nullif(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 0) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS gross_profit_margin_pct FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL;
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32% for the period from October 2025 through September 2026. This is based on a total gross profit of $1,584,502.69 AUD on $2,716,823.41 AUD in revenue (excluding GST). Please note that this calculation excludes any order lines that did not have a recorded cost.
results.assumptions: Calculated across all non-voided orders over the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Revenue is taken ex-GST (divided by 1.1) to compare against ex-GST unit costs. Order lines with NULL costs were excluded.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, round(sum(((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * l.quantity)), 2) AS gross_profit FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY gross_profit DESC LIMIT 5
results.answer: Your top five products by gross profit are the One-Piece Swimsuit at $165,884.48, Shirt Dress at $130,441.22, Straw Hat at $108,854.01, High-Rise Jeans at $104,531.12, and Wool Coat at $89,912.11 AUD. These figures exclude GST and any product variants that were missing a recorded unit cost.
results.assumptions: Calculated gross profit as (line revenue ex-GST) minus (unit cost ex-GST * quantity) for all non-voided orders. Variants with a NULL cost were excluded.

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(o.total), 0) - (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM refunds), 2) AS net_revenue FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: Your net revenue after refunds is $3,205,298.79 AUD. This total is based on all non-voided orders minus all recorded refunds across the available data. Please note this figure assumes all historical refund records were fully captured in the provided dataset.
results.assumptions: Net revenue is calculated as total revenue from all non-voided orders minus total refund amounts across all recorded data.

results.question: What percentage of orders had a refund?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT r.order_id) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 0) AS NUMERIC), 2) AS refund_percentage FROM orders o LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: Around 5.7% of your orders had a refund. This calculation is based on non-voided orders that have at least one associated refund in the database.
results.assumptions: Calculated the percentage of non-voided orders that have at least one associated refund in the database.

results.question: Which product has had the most units refunded, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(rl.quantity) AS units_refunded FROM refund_lines rl JOIN order_lines ol ON rl.order_line_id = ol.order_line_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_refunded DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: The product with the most units refunded is the One-Piece Swimsuit, with a total of 165 units refunded. This count excludes any voided orders to ensure the data is accurate. Please note that this is based on the available sales data and reflects the exact results returned for your shop.
results.assumptions: Excluding voided orders by joining the orders table and filtering out financial_status = 'voided' when calculating refunded units.

results.question: How many different customers have placed an order?
results.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers_with_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL;
results.answer: A total of 2,909 different customers have placed an order. This count is based on unique customer IDs from non-voided orders. Please note that this total excludes orders placed as guests and may count the same person multiple times if they used different checkout details.
results.assumptions: Counted unique customer IDs from non-voided orders. Note that many orders are placed by guests (NULL customer_id), and customers may appear under multiple IDs if they checked out with different details.

results.question: What percentage of orders were placed by guests with no customer account?
results.sql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 END) / count(*), 2) AS guest_order_percentage FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided';
results.answer: Guests without a customer account placed 22.47% of your non-voided orders. This calculation only includes completed orders that were not voided.
results.assumptions: Calculated the percentage of non-voided orders where customer_id is NULL (guest checkout) out of all non-voided orders.

results.question: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(orders.total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE orders.financial_status <> 'voided' AND orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
results.answer: Your revenue for the last three complete months was $367,315.71 in June, $342,251.10 in July, and $282,129.97 in August 2026. These figures include all non-voided orders and are based on Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Treating today as 2026-09-30. The last 3 complete months are June, July, and August 2026. Revenue is the sum of orders.total for non-voided orders, attributed to the order creation date in Australia/Sydney time.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql:
WITH eofy_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        'EOFY Sale (19 Jun - 5 Jul)' AS period,
        SUM(total) AS total_revenue,

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation is based on all refund events recorded between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Calculated the average time difference in days between the order creation date and the refund creation date for all refund events. Data range covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?

results.answer: Orders that used a discount brought in a total of $944,363.46 in revenue. This calculation includes all non-voided orders where a discount was applied.

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') IN (6, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, round(sum(o.total), 2) AS revenue, count(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more revenue than weekends, with weekdays generating $2,147,980.22 across 11,153 orders compared to $1,173,950.49 from 6,187 orders on weekends. This comparison assumes all orders created in Australia/Sydney local time, excluding voided orders, accurately represent your sales performance.
results.assumptions: Compared total revenue and order counts between weekends (Saturday and Sunday) and weekdays (Monday through Friday) using orders created in Australia/Sydney local time, excluding voided orders.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH ranked_products AS (SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, p.title AS product_title, sum(ol.quantity) AS total_units_sold, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(ol.quantity) DESC) AS rn FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type), p.title) SELECT product_type, product_title AS best_selling_product, total_units_sold FROM ranked_products WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY product_type;
results.answer: Your best-selling product overall is the One-Piece Swimsuit in swimwear with 4,043 units sold, while the Merino Crew Jumper leads knitwear with 526 units. The top sellers for the remaining categories are the Straw Hat (accessories), Shirt Dress (dress), Wool Coat (outerwear), High-Rise Jeans (pants), Linen Wrap Skirt (skirt), and Ribbed Tank (top). These figures reflect total units sold per product type, assuming all recorded transactions are complete and accurate.
results.assumptions: Replaced the USING clause with explicit ON clauses to avoid potential syntax errors in the SQL parser.
